title: John Snow's Cholera Map (1854)
explainer: In 1854, physician John Snow plotted cholera deaths from an outbreak in London's Soho neighborhood directly onto a street map rather than just tabulating them, and the resulting cluster of cases pointed straight at a single contaminated water pump on Broad Street. It's one of the earliest and most famous examples of a simple data visualization settling a real-world, high-stakes question — the same instinct behind the applied statistics in this lesson: put the data in front of your eyes and look for the pattern.
